Why the river bends

Field notes, spring survey

Rivers rarely run straight for long. A small bump on one bank slows the water there, and the faster water on the opposite side cuts the outer bank a little deeper each season. Over years the bend grows, and the inside of the curve collects sand where the current is slow.

We measured the outer bank at twelve stations along a single meander. The deepest cut sat just downstream of the apex, which matches what the slower inside flow would predict.

What we changed

This season we added two stations below the apex and moved the gauge away from the willow roots, which had been shading the sensor in the afternoon.
